title: Landfalling northwest Pacific typhoons kept their 1977-2013 intensity rise in 2014-2024 in JTWC and JMA best tracks, but their intensification rate stopped rising and local SST did not predict it
abstract: Question: did the intensification of landfalling northwest Pacific typhoons that Mei and Xie (2016) found for 1977-2013 continue, and did its stated mechanism (faster intensification tied to local sea surface temperature, SST) continue? Approach: we used IBTrACS v04r01 JTWC and adjusted JMA best tracks and the paper's methods, including a four-cluster track regression mixture fitted jointly to both agencies. We wrote the plan before the test, fitted all models on the paper's years and froze them, then compared 2014-2024 (JTWC) and 2014-2025 (JMA) with the extended trends. Results: the replication was close (basin lifetime peak intensity, LPI, +13.2% in 1977-2014; paper 14%; cluster 1+2 intensification rate +1.53 m/s per 6 h; paper 1.5). The mostly landfalling clusters 1+2 had a mean LPI of 56.0 m/s (JTWC, 95 typhoons) and 57.1 m/s (JMA) in the new years, against trend forecasts of 56.6 and 56.4 m/s and a 1977-2013 mean of 51 m/s; the trend forecast halved the squared error of a no-change forecast. The intensification rate did not continue to increase: cluster 1+2 rates were 3.40 and 4.04 m/s per 6 h against trend forecasts of 3.99 and 4.51, and cluster 1 rates were below the trend in both agencies (p = 0.044 and 0.010). Local July-November SST continued to warm (+0.46 C above the 1977-2013 mean), but a frozen SST model did not follow the year-to-year rate in the new years (r = 0.12 and -0.24) and predicted LPI 2-5 m/s too low. Typhoons without land contact were below their trend (p = 0.048 and 0.018). Conclusion: the high intensity of landfalling typhoons continued, but not through a still faster intensification, and the local SST link did not predict the new years. Limitations: 11-12 new seasons give wide intervals and cannot separate a continued trend from a level step for cluster 1; tests are not corrected for multiplicity; the JMA conversion uses a linear fit to the Koba table; our clusters are a reimplementation.
